title: What you don’t do, and when

fn.en: Say what you don’t do, tell the time and agree a time to meet.

items.s: The meeting starts at nine and I arrived at nine. I was ___. ✅
I arrived at half past nine. I was ___. ⏩
I arrived at half past eight. I was ___. ⏪
I can’t talk now — I’m very ___. 📅
I have no plans this evening. I’m ___. 🆓

lines: I never work [at|in|on] Sunday, and I hardly ever work [in|at|on] the evening.
We usually have lunch [at|in|on] midday and I go to bed [at|in|on] midnight.

sub.en: Look at the sentences. What form is the verb after don’t and doesn’t?

items.q: I ___ go to classes in the evening.
Chris ___ have a shower in the morning.
items.why: he / she / it → doesn’t. The -s is already in doesn’t, so the verb loses it.

items.q: They ___ a lot of free time.
Astronauts ___ special clothes in the space station.
She ___ late. She’s always on time.
items.why: RECYCLED: the frequency word goes after am / is / are.

items.q: “Are you free after class?” — “Sorry, I ___ this evening.”

items.a: I don’t work at the weekend

items.from: She takes the bus to work.
items.a: She doesn’t take the bus to work

items.from: He has a shower in the morning.
items.a: He doesn’t have a shower in the morning

items.from: They speak to their families every day.
items.a: They don’t speak to their families every day
My sister doesn’t do the housework

tts: Most astronauts don’t feel well when they first go into space. Space sickness is very common.
Astronauts don’t wear special clothes in the space station. They only need a space suit when they go on a spacewalk.
Astronauts don’t change their clothes every day. It isn’t possible to wash clothes in space.
Astronauts usually exercise for two hours a day.
Usually, an astronaut doesn’t go on a spacewalk more than once a week.

items.s: Most astronauts feel well at the start.
Astronauts wear special clothes inside the space station.
They need a space suit for a spacewalk.
They change their clothes every day.
They exercise about two hours a day.
An astronaut usually goes on a spacewalk every day.

use: Would you like to go out for a pizza?
tts: Are you free after class today? I’m sorry, but I’m busy this evening. But I don’t have any plans tomorrow.
Would you like to go out for a pizza? Yes, I’d love to. What time shall we meet?
Eight o’clock at Gino’s? Or do you want to meet at the station? Yes, let’s meet there at 7.45.

items.sit: You are in the street and you want to know the time.
o: Excuse me, what time is it?
Excuse me, what is the clock?
Excuse me, how time is it?

items.sit: Your phone says 6:10 and someone asks the time.
Your colleague never works on Sunday.
A friend asks: “Would you like to go out for a pizza?” You want to go.
A friend asks if you are free this evening. You have a lot of work.
o: Sorry, I don’t free this evening.
Sorry, I’m busy in this evening.

lines.s: Sorry, I’m ___ this evening. But tomorrow is fine. 📅
Great. Would you like to go for a pizza?

write.q: Write 6 sentences: three things you don’t do in a normal week, the time you start and finish work, and one invitation with a time.
write.model: I don’t work at the weekend and I don’t take the bus — I walk. My brother doesn’t drink coffee, so we always meet in a tea house. I start work at nine and I finish at six. I’m never late. Are you free on Friday? Let’s meet at quarter past seven at the station.

speak.q: Say out loud: three things you don’t do, the time now, and an invitation. Then refuse one politely.
speak.model: I don’t work on Sunday. I don’t drive. My sister doesn’t eat meat. It’s twenty to five. Are you free after work? — Sorry, I’m busy this evening. Maybe tomorrow?
